soṇakāyana.notes: Sikhāmoggallāna reports the student's words in AN 4.234. AN 4.233 is a neighboring discourse on deeds. AN 4.242 names Soṇakāyana in the chapter summary.

soṇā.notes: AN 1.241 names the nun foremost in energy. Thig 5.8 names her in the attribution and recalls her ten children and late ordination. AN 8.91–117 lists the laywoman and her mother separately. AN 6.55, SN 22.49–50, SN 35.128, and Ud 5.6 concern men named Soṇa. The AN 1 groups on either side of AN 1.241 and AN 8.118–119 are page overlaps.

subha.notes: All three dialogues call the student Todeyya's son. MN 99 also recounts his meeting with Jāṇussoṇi. The imported MN 29 and MN 30 references miss this episode. The Subhās in Thig 13.5 and 14.1 are nuns.

subhadda.notes: DN 16 needs three different identifications within one discourse. The deceased lay follower is named at 2.6.13, the wanderer at Kusinārā at 5.23.1, and the monk who welcomes the Buddha's death at 6.20.1. A single entry for DN 16 would misidentify the other two. SN 55.10 names the lay follower at Ñātika. The page placements at SN 55.5–6 miss him. DN 17 names Queen Subhaddā.

subhagavana.notes: DN 14, MN 1, and MN 49 locate the wood at Ukkaṭṭhā. SN 6.4 is a parallel to the Baka episode set at Jetavana, as the entry observes. SN 6.3 concerns Brahmadeva. MN 99 refers to the forest through Pokkharasāti's epithet subhagavaniko.

subhā.notes: The only candidate describes deities. MN 120:20.6–8 lists all three constituent classes under their full names. The nun of Jīvaka's mango grove in Thig 14.1 and the smith's daughter in Thig 13.5 have no candidate biography. DN 10 and MN 99 refer to the male student Subha.

subāhu.notes: Thag 1.52 is the elder's own verse about the roofed hut. Its attribution has the joined form Subāhutthero, so it falls outside the packet's eligible IDs. Thag 1.60:2.1–2 lists him with Godhika, Valliya, and Uttiya in the chapter summary. Sīvali composed the verse in Thag 1.60.

sucimukhī.notes: The wanderer questions Sāriputta about how he eats in SN 28.10. SN 28.8–9 are neighboring discourses. The summary at SN 28.10:7.6 also gives her name with a long ū, sūcimukhī.

sudassana.notes: MN 116:4.5 names the independent Buddha at Isigili. The chronology and the encounters at Cāvalapabbata in the entry come from its other sources. In SN 3.13 Pasenadi asks Sudassana to repeat the Buddha's verse at meals. SN 3.14 is a battle narrative. Neither candidate describes the mountain.

sudatta.notes: AN 1.249 explicitly calls Anāthapiṇḍika Sudatta. His biography is under the separate headword Anāthapiṇḍika. DN 16 and SN 55.8 identify the once-returner of Ñātika. For Sudatta 07 the cited verse exchange is SN 2.16, where the local text calls the godling Vāsudatta. For Sudatta 11, Thag 1.37 identifies the elder as Kumāputta's friend, with Sudatta supplied by the entry. Neither passage is in the eligible list. The summaries in AN 4.60 and SN 10.12 point back to the householder's discourses, AN 4.58 and SN 10.8.

suddhikabhāradvāja.notes: SN 7.7 names the brahmin and gives the exchange on purification. SN 7.5–6 concern other brahmins. The chapter summary at SN 7.10:18.4 recalls him by the shorter name Suddhika.

sugandha.notes: Alongside the attribution at Thag 1.24:1.5, the chapter summary names Sugandha at Thag 1.30:2.2. The packet misses that second occurrence.

sujāta.notes: The packet misses Sundarī's father in Thig 13.4. The Pali names Sujāta at 11.3, 12.5, and 13.5, one segment before the name in each English rendering. SN 21.5 praises a monk called Sujāta. DPPN itself treats his identity with the father as uncertain. SN 21.4 is a page overlap. The remaining packet mentions are women named Sujātā. The former Buddha has no candidate.

sujātā.notes: AN 1.258 names Seniyadhītā as foremost in going for refuge. Despite the DPD hint and the citation for Sujātā 06, the named woman in DN 16:2.6–7 is the deceased stream-enterer of Ñātika. DN 16:4.42 mentions the pre-awakening meal without naming its donor. AN 7.63 identifies Anāthapiṇḍika's daughter-in-law. Thig 6.4 names a nun with no candidate entry. The neighboring AN 1 groups, SN 55.7, and AN 7.62 are page overlaps.

sukkā.notes: DN 20:17.1–2 names the Sukkā among the gods arriving with the Veghanasā. Sujato translates Sukkā as the gods of Venus, and DN 20 is missing from the eligible list. The Pali summary at SN 10.12:14.4 also recalls the two Sukkā discourses about the nun. SN 10.8 concerns Sudatta.

sumana.notes: AN 6.49 names Khema's companion at Andhavana. The citation lands at AN 6.44, the discourse with Migasālā. DPPN suggests either of two elders as a possible identification. Neither Thag 5.4 nor Thag 6.10 connects its author with Khema. DN 32 names the yakkha chief beside Pajjunna and Sumukha. The AN 5, AN 8, and Therīgāthā mentions are feminine Sumanā.

sumanā.notes: The full entry covers both the princess of AN 5.31 and, on the authority of the Therīgāthā commentary, the nun of verse 16. Thig 1.16 calls her Sumanā who went forth in old age. Thig 1.14 has a separate attribution. AN 8.91–117 lists a laywoman named Sumanā without a royal title. SN 3.1 records the talk to Pasenadi, while her attendance comes from the commentary. AN 5.30 and AN 8.89–90 are page overlaps. AN 6.49 names a male monk.

sumaṅgala.notes: The packet misses the elder's name in the chapter summary at Thag 1.50:2.2.

sumbha.notes: SN 46.30 places Udāyī in Sumbha country. Where the entry gives the town as Desaka with a query, SN 46.30:1.1 reads Setaka and SN 47.19–20 read Sedaka. SN 46.29 is a page overlap.

sunakkhatta.notes: The entry reverses part of Sunakkhatta's criticism. In MN 12:2.5 he acknowledges that practicing the teaching leads to the complete ending of suffering. At 4.3–5 the Buddha calls this inadvertent praise. MN 11 is a page overlap.
